title: feat: rewrite shinycannon in TypeScript
description:
## Summary

Complete rewrite of shinycannon from Kotlin/JVM to TypeScript/Node.js. This is a 1:1 behavioral rewrite — same recording format, same CSV output format (compatible with shinyloadtest R package).

**CLI change:** Load testing is now behind the `loadtest` subcommand to make room for future subcommands (`record`, `report`).

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f375ce4d-8b1a-4754-8410-1137daa4124a)

**Key changes:**
- **Runtime:** Kotlin/JVM → Node.js 20+ with TypeScript strict mode
- **Distribution:** Maven/Docker/fpm → `npm install shinycannon` / `npx shinycannon`
- **Dependencies:** 3 runtime deps (`ws`, `tough-cookie`, `commander`)
- **Build:** `tsup` (esbuild) producing ESM bundle
- **Tests:** 173 tests across 15 test files (vitest) covering unit, integration, and behavioral constraints

**Architecture:** 13 focused modules (types, recording, tokens, sockjs, url, http, websocket, detect, auth, logger, output, session, worker, cli, main, ui) with discriminated unions for event types, per-session cookie jars, and async queue-based WebSocket message buffering.

**Behavioral parity:** All 12 behavioral constraints from the original Kotlin implementation are preserved and tested (recording validation, status code handling, WS queue bounds, key matching, output format, etc.).

## Verification

```bash
npm install
npx shinycannon loadtest --help
npx shinycannon loadtest recording.log https://your-app.example.com --workers 5 --loaded-duration-minutes 2
```

All CI checks (lint, typecheck, build, test) pass.

title: Address review comments on --receive-queue-size feature
WIP: Jupyter widget / shinywidgets support
description:
## Summary

- Fix `replaceTokens` to ignore JavaScript template literals in minified widget code (plotly ESM bundles contain `${D}`, `${E}`, etc. that were falsely matched as shinycannon tokens)
- Recognize Python Shiny's empty message format (`{"values":{}}` with objects) in `canIgnore`, not just R Shiny's format (`{"values":[]}` with arrays)
- Remove dead JCenter repository from `pom.xml`, bump `kotlin-argparser` 2.0.3 → 2.0.7

## Still TODO

Comm ID mapping for Jupyter widgets — see `jupyter-widget-support.md` for full writeup. During playback, `comm_id` values assigned by the server differ from those in the recording, so `WS_SEND` messages that reference comm IDs will send stale values. The proposed fix is to capture a `recorded_comm_id → actual_comm_id` mapping from `shinywidgets_comm_open` messages and apply it to outgoing messages.

## Test plan

- [ ] Reproduce with `python-example-nba` from `shinyloadtest-example` repo (`run_test.sh`)
- [ ] Verify "illegal tokens" error is gone
- [ ] Verify empty message no longer causes queue desync
- [ ] Implement and test comm_id mapping (future work)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Bump `receiveQueue` limit from 5 to 50
description:
Example 

```
2021-11-22 13:06:27.713 ERROR [thread06] - Playback failed: receiveQueue is full (max = 5)
java.lang.Exception: receiveQueue is full (max = 5)
```

Previously, the queue had a size of `5`. Now it is set to `50`. 

--------------------------------

If app authors are sending enough non-deterministic custom messages to hit the new limit, I'd love to see what the app is doing and how we could address it.

title: Misc fixes
description:
This PR fixes two problems discovered by a customer.

1. **Target URL slash-dropping** Unfortunately, the [uribuilder-tiny](https://github.com/moznion/uribuilder-tiny) library we used for URL manipulation in shinycannon did not conserve a trailing slash on the target URL if one was provided. This caused shinycannon to fail for the customer the way shinyloadtest did [until we fixed it](https://github.com/rstudio/shinyloadtest/pull/119). This PR addresses the problem conservatively by introducing a `joinPaths()` function containing the same logic the analogous function in shinyloadtest does. I call this approach conservative because there's a decent argument for either rolling our own URL builder, or for putting together a PR on `uribuilder-tiny`, but either would involve considerably more work.
2. **Status check bug** It's an error if an HTTP status code encountered during playback does not match one that was recorded, with the exception of 304 and 200 - they are considered equivalent to account for browser caching. The problem with the previous logic was when a code during recording was NOT 304 or 200, and was something else - like 404. A 404 encountered during recording is not necessarily a show-stopping error, and so 4xx requests are recorded like any other. shinycannon just expects to see the same code at playback time. However, even if the 404 was also encountered during playback, shinycannon considered 404 != 404, which made no sense. So, this PR simplifies the previous (confusing and wrong) set logic into a series of `==` checks.

title: File/directory handling tweaks
description:
There are two minor changes here that make interaction with the recording file and output directory more intuitive.

## 1. If the recording file doesn't exist, don't create the output directory.

Previously, even if the specified recording file didn't exist, an error was printed and `shinycannon` would exit. However, the output directory would still be created, and populated with `debug.log` if `--debug-log` was specified.

Shalu and I both found this counter-intuitive. It didn't make sense for an output directory to be created when there was no possible interesting output data to store.

Now, existence of the file is checked before any output directory or log files are created, and `shinycannon` exits immediately without creating any directories or files if the recording file doesn't exist.

## 2. Respect `--overwrite-output`.

Previously, even if `--overwrite-output` was specified -- indicating that the output directory should be deleted and recreated even it exists already -- `shinycannon` would still refuse to delete the output directory if it didn't contain files that an output directory normally would contain.

The original idea with this was, we would have this extra safeguard ensuring people didn't accidentally delete directories that contained important data unrelated to shinycannon. In practice though, it's just annoying.

Since the user is explicitly specifying `--overwrite-output`, we should assume they know what they're doing, and not confuse them with an error message.

title: Simplify app detection, fixes #38
description:
Before playing a recording against a target application, we attempt to determine the type of the server hosting the app. We use that information to print a nice message if the server type is unsupported, or if it doesn't match the type of server the recording was created with.

The determination is made with a series of heuristics involving inspection of response headers, cookies, and interpretation of a response body's HTML.

(shinyloadtest applies identical logic to encode the server type in the recording before creating a recording file)

Previously, the last heuristic applied would look for `shiny.min.js` or `shiny.js` `<script>` tags in the markup by parsing the HTML, searching with xpath, and then comparing the `src` attribute string by regex.

As evidenced by #38, this approach turned out to be too heavy-handed, because functional Shiny apps don't necessarily produce markup we are able to parse.

So, in this PR, we simplify looking for the scripts. Now, the check is regex-only, and no HTML is parsed.

*The corresponding PR in shinyloadtest is rstudio/shinyloadtest#115*

title: Fix playback error triggered by empty extendsession POST request
description:
## The Problem

@shalutiwari reported a long-running load test triggered an error like the following that terminated the test prematurely, and I was able to reproduce:

```
2019-07-25 16:05:52.096 ERROR [thread05] - Playback failed: Entity may not be null
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Entity may not be null
        at org.apache.http.util.Args.notNull(Args.java:54)2019-07-25 16:05:52.102 INFO [thread05] - Stopped
```

The debug log showed the following stack trace:

```
2019-07-25 02:34:49.799 ERROR [thread03] - Playback failed: Entity may not be null
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Entity may not be null
	at org.apache.http.util.Args.notNull(Args.java:54)
	at org.apache.http.util.EntityUtils.toString(EntityUtils.java:307)
	at com.rstudio.shinycannon.Event$Http$REQ_POST$handle$1.invoke(Events.kt:236)
	at com.rstudio.shinycannon.Event$Http$REQ_POST$handle$1.invoke(Events.kt:206)
	at com.rstudio.shinycannon.Event.withLog(Events.kt:71)
	at com.rstudio.shinycannon.Event$Http$REQ_POST.handle(Events.kt:212)
	at com.rstudio.shinycannon.ShinySession.run(Main.kt:185)
	at com.rstudio.shinycannon.EnduranceTest$run$4.invoke(Main.kt:307)
	at com.rstudio.shinycannon.EnduranceTest$run$4.invoke$default(Main.kt:299)
	at com.rstudio.shinycannon.EnduranceTest$run$6.invoke(Main.kt:330)
	at com.rstudio.shinycannon.EnduranceTest$run$6.invoke(Main.kt:251)
	at kotlin.concurrent.ThreadsKt$thread$thread$1.run(Thread.kt:30)
```

The stack trace involves our handling of the `REQ_POST` event, which caused me to look for any `REQ_POST`s in the recording. There is one like this:

```
{"type":"REQ_POST","begin":"2019-07-18T18:15:18.341Z","end":"2019-07-18T18:15:19.005Z","status":204,"url":"/_w_${WORKER}/__extendsession__"}
```

## The Reason

This is the offending code from the end of the method that handles `REQ_POST`:

https://github.com/rstudio/shinycannon/blob/60221b96534321d00d9672a149125a9da0fa44d4/src/main/kotlin/com/rstudio/shinycannon/Events.kt#L235-L242

When a `REQ_POST` is handled, we [`check`](https://kotlinlang.org/api/latest/jvm/stdlib/kotlin/check.html) that the HTTP response code received from the target server matches the response code contained in the recording. If the check fails, an exception is thrown with a message string that includes some request details, including the body of the response as a string.

There were two problems with this checking code that resulted in the error:

1. `response.entity` was null because there was no response body in the case of the `__extendsession__` request, and according to the [documentation for `EntityUtils.toString()`](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-core-ga/httpcore/apidocs/org/apache/http/util/EntityUtils.html#toString(org.apache.http.HttpEntity)) the entity must not be `null`.
1. `EntityUtils.toString()` was being called after every `REQ_POST`, even if the status code was correct. This was unnecessary, and potentially expensive, and the reason we were seeing the error even on successful requests.

## The Fix

1. Ensure `EntityUtils.toString()` is only ever called with a non-null argument
1. Move construction of the `body` string to within the `check` block

title: Remove the app URL query string before constructing the websocket URL
description:
This fixes an error that occurs when one attempts to load test an application that has query parameters in its URL (such as when URL bookmarking is used). The parameters must be stripped in order to construct the correct Websocket URL.

Refs trello https://trello.com/c/t9LGKYh5/1200-shinycannon-query-bookmark-error-error-thread01-playback-failed-the-status-code-of-the-opening-handshake-response-is-not-101-swi

title: Consolidate cookie/header massage code; fix SSP detection
description:
Previously one of the SSP detection heuristics was to look for the `ssp-xsrf` header in the initial request's response.

This was wrong, because SSP actually sends the header `x-ssp-xsrf`. `SSP-XSRF` is the name of the cookie it sends.

Note that header names are case sensitive but cookie names are not. Throughout the code, headers are normalized to lower-case.

This change fixes SSP detection by looking for the `x-ssp-xsrf` header, and augments the heuristic by additionally looking for the `SSP-XSRF` cookie.

Refs Trello: https://trello.com/c/pNDKc7DC/1114-shinycannon-ssp-detection-broken

title: Fix SSP detection
description:
#36 broke SSP detection because headers in the detection response weren't being downcased, and we were looking for lowercase header names.

It was working for non-authenticated apps, which is how it probably slipped past us, because our first heuristic (looking for SSP-XSRF) was working. With auth on, there is no SSP-XSRF during our detection request, and our second heuristic (looking for `x-powered-by`) failed because the actual header was cased `X-Powered-By`.

This fixes the problem by lower-casing headers before we start working with them.

title: Unlimited error message length and clean up imports
description:
Certain messages were being truncated because a recent change to the logging limited errors to 80 characters.

I originally thought to limit messages this way because one kind of error message, printed when the status code from a request differs from what was expected in the recording, prints the entire response body. It results in a wall of text at the console.

In this change, I simply bring back unlimited-length messages, since we definitely don't want most errors to be truncated. Separately, in the future, we should revisit how we want to preserve responses to aid in debugging. My current thinking is that the log is not the place for them, and that perhaps we should write them to their own files in the output directory if debugging mode is on.

The PR also does some Intellij cleanup of the Java imports.

title: Java 7 compatibility fixes
description:
# Rationale

Currently, JRE 8+ (aka 1.8) is required on all platforms. Running on Java 7 (aka 1.7) results in at least the following error:
```
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: java/time/Instant
```

Java 7 compatibility is nice because it means that people on Ubuntu 14.04 (LTS, EOL April 2019) would only need to install our `.deb` and not worry about manually installing the Oracle JRE 8 (there isn't an OpenJDK 8 for Ubuntu 14.04).

As an alternative to this PR, we could instead add instructions for running on Ubuntu 14.04 to our documentation that would include steps for downloading Oracle JRE 8.

# Approach

The PR:
- Configures Kotlin to produce 1.6+ compatible bytecode (this was already happening since 1.6 is the default, but now it's explicit)
- Downgrades log4j from 2.11.1 to 2.8.2, since 2.8.2 was the last release with 1.7-compatible class files.
- Uses `kotlin-stdlib-jdk7` instead of `kotlin-stdlib`
- Introduces joda-time for its org.joda.time.Instant type instead of relying on 1.8's java.time.Instant. 
- Replaces use of ConcurrentHashMap.replaceAll to track stats with a synchronized block in which vars are mutated.

# Risks

I had to downgrade our log4j dep to 2.8.2 (released April 2017) from 2.11.1 and there are quite a few [changes between the two](https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.0/changes-report.html). I've done some testing and everything seems to still work, but there's a chance our logging stuff is now broken in some subtle way.

title: Console brevity
description:
High-dimensional logging configuration hell was entered in order to upgrade Log4j to v2, because v2
has more output formatting options, including 2 we really wanted: ability to truncate messages
over a certain length for console display, and ability to display short stacktraces at the console.

However, upgrading log4j meant updating the code we used to programmatically configure logging.
Also, various magic tricks in the slf4j and log4j 1 jars which automagically got us log events
out of Apache HttpClient stopped working.

We didn't want to punt on Apache HttpClient events, because HTTP activity is an important
thing to have in debug.log.

In order to get the Apache events back we had to:

1. Exclude commons-logging from httpclient in pom.xml
2. Add jcl-over-slf4j dependency
3. Add log4j-slf4j dependency

After all that, we got 2 new features:

1. Console log messages are limited to 50 characters by truncating to the right
1. Instead of not being printed at all, the first line of stack traces are printed at the console
    - Full stack traces continue to be printed to debug.log if enabled

title: Emit CLI args as JSON at the 2nd line of session CSVs
description:
We already add the CLI arguments as a comment at the top of session recording `.csv` files. This enhancement adds an additional comment line that contains a JSON object representing the arguments.

The tops of session files now look like this:

```
alandipert@frito~/g/r/s/q/sessions➜ head -10 0_0_0.csv
# http://localhost:3838/sample-apps/hello/ --workers 10 --output-dir qa-425 --overwrite-output
# {"appUrl":"http://localhost:3838/sample-apps/hello/","debugLog":false,"loadedDurationMinutes":0.0,"logLevel":"WARN","outputDir":"qa-425","overwriteOutput":true,"recordingPath":"../shinyloadtest/recording.log","workers":10}
session_id,worker_id,iteration,event,timestamp,input_line_number,comment
0,0,0,PLAYER_SESSION_CREATE,1537482856562,0,
0,0,0,REQ_HOME_START,1537482856562,3,
0,0,0,REQ_HOME_END,1537482857590,3,
0,0,0,REQ_GET_START,1537482857590,4,
0,0,0,PLAYBACK_FAIL,1537482857660,4,
```

Doing this, I realized it's kind of weird that we're putting argument information at the top of every CSV instead of into a single special-purpose metadata file in the recording output directory. We might consider doing that instead in the future.

title: Exit summary
description:
(should be merged after #13)

Currently, the thread that prints status output prints a line every 5 seconds. Because it's on a timer, it might not be the last thing to produce output, and so when `shinycannon` exits it's not obvious that it exited normally or what the final stats were.

This adds a line to the console output with final stats right before exiting the JVM, making it clear that the program is shutting down, and how many completed/failed sessions there were.

Before, the last few lines of output might look like this:
```
...
2018-09-11 13:35:13.583 INFO [progress] - Running: 4, Failed: 0, Done: 6
2018-09-11 13:35:13.796 INFO [thread07] - Stopped
2018-09-11 13:35:14.863 INFO [thread08] - Stopped
2018-09-11 13:35:15.796 INFO [thread09] - Stopped
2018-09-11 13:35:16.939 INFO [thread10] - Stopped
$
```
Now, the last few lines look like this:
```
...
2018-09-11 13:35:13.583 INFO [progress] - Running: 4, Failed: 0, Done: 6
2018-09-11 13:35:13.796 INFO [thread07] - Stopped
2018-09-11 13:35:14.863 INFO [thread08] - Stopped
2018-09-11 13:35:15.796 INFO [thread09] - Stopped
2018-09-11 13:35:16.939 INFO [thread10] - Stopped
2018-09-11 13:35:16.939 INFO [thread00] - Complete. Failed: 0, Done: 10
$
```

title: Better error message when recording file is missing
description:
Prior to this PR, shinycannon emits a cryptic error when the specified recording file doesn't exist:

```
SHINYCANNON_USER=pamtest SHINYCANNON_PASS=pamtest shinycannon recording/centos7_pamauth_05_r.log http://192.168.40.5:3838/05_sliders/ --workers 5 --output-dir centos705pamtestrec_playback_onubuntu18 
Exception in thread "thread00" java.lang.IllegalStateException: Check failed.
    at com.rstudio.shinycannon.MainKt$main$1.invoke(Main.kt:396)
    at com.rstudio.shinycannon.MainKt$main$1.invoke(Main.kt)
    at com.xenomachina.argparser.SystemExitExceptionKt.mainBody(SystemExitException.kt:71)
    at com.xenomachina.argparser.SystemExitExceptionKt.mainBody$default(SystemExitException.kt:69)
    at com.rstudio.shinycannon.MainKt.main(Main.kt:380)
```

Now, the error looks like this if the recording doesn't exist or if it points to a directory instead of a file:

```
alandipert@frito~/g/r/shinycannon➜ java -jar target/shinycannon-1.0.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar reciording.log https://beta.rstudioconnect.com/content/3843/ --workers 1 --log-level info --output-dir test --overwrite-output
Exception in thread "thread00" java.lang.IllegalStateException: recording 'reciording.log' doesn't exist or is not a file
	at com.rstudio.shinycannon.MainKt$main$1.invoke(Main.kt:398)
	at com.rstudio.shinycannon.MainKt$main$1.invoke(Main.kt)
	at com.xenomachina.argparser.SystemExitExceptionKt.mainBody(SystemExitException.kt:71)
	at com.xenomachina.argparser.SystemExitExceptionKt.mainBody$default(SystemExitException.kt:69)
	at com.rstudio.shinycannon.MainKt.main(Main.kt:380)
```

title: Custom user-agent string
description:
shinycannon now reports a `user-agent` of `shinycannon/<version>`, where `<version>` looks like `1.0.0-22cb125` or similar.

Should be merged after #11.

title: Report version in help output and in output directories
description:
This bakes a `shinycannon-version.txt` file containing a string like `1.0.0-46d4735` into the jar at build-time. That makes the version number and git sha available at runtime where it can be seen by:
- `shinycannon -h` (it appears at the end of output)
- Running and inspecting `<output-dir>/shinycannon-version.txt`

This PR also:
- Adds a flag to produce`<output-dir>/debug.log` instead of always writing it, because it can get huge (hundreds of MBs for 60 workers for 5 minutes)
- Fixes a hang caused by hung timer thread in the websocket library by explicitly terminating the JVM when the run is complete (https://github.com/TakahikoKawasaki/nv-websocket-client/issues/140)
- Fixes a typo in the Makefile

title: Fix debug logging calls
description:
These calls were valid with the old kotlin logging lib API we used to use because it expected a "block", but the Java logging API we're using now just casts the block to a string, producing nonsense like this:

`DEBUG [ReadingThread] 2018-08-08 01:39:22,651 (Events.kt:265) - Function0<java.lang.String>`

Now, we're back to just logging strings, and the messages show up in debug.log again.

title: Better error handling
description:
The original idea with this PR was to just improve Websocket error handling, but that mission evolved into a slightly larger re-work of what happens with errors and warnings generally.

Now:

1. `ShinySession` instances have a `failure` interrupt (an instance variable of type `Throwable?`). At the start of every iteration of that session's run loop inside the `run` method, `failure` is checked for non-nullness. If it's non-null, the `Throwable` is logged, stats updated, and the loop is terminated. The `run` method returns, which causes the orchestrating machinery to start a new session in that thread.
1. If a `WS_RECV` or `WS_RECV_INIT` type message takes longer than 10 seconds to arrive, a note is logged at the `WARN` level every 10 seconds until the message arrives. These will show up in the console output because the default log level is warn. `shinycannon` has hung inexplicably; hopefully this feature will make such hangs easier to diagnose. Example: ` WARN [Thread-1] 2018-08-10 08:40:46,401 (Events.kt:317) - WS_RECV line 37: Waited 10 seconds for message and didn't receive one. Waiting longer..`
1. If a message handler throws an exception, shinycannon won't crash. Instead, that session is "failed" cleanly.
1. Kotlin was upgraded to to 1.2.60
1. `debug.log` no longer contains duplicate messages. This was happening because in the root/app logger hierarchy, the app-level logger was both appending a message to `debug.log` and passing it to its parent, the root logger, which did the same. Setting `additivity = false` in the app logger config prevents the message from bubbling to the root logger.

## Items to improve

These came up during today's (2018-08-10) check-in.

- [x] WS_RECV/WS_RECV_INIT "hung" warning message should show up after 30 seconds instead of 10 seconds. It should also show the cumulative time spent waiting.
- [x] Console output shouldn't include Kotlin file and line numbers
- [x] Console output should start with the timestamp
- [x] Console output columns, except for the message string, should be the same length. Currently `[main]` and `[Thread-0]` etc don't behave.
- [x] `main` thread should instead be called `thread00`
- [x] Worker threads should be numbered starting from 1

## Example run with these enhancements

```
alan@gazebo~/g/r/shinycannon➜ java -jar target/shinycannon-1.0.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar 1minute_patched2.log http://localhost:3838/01_hello/ --workers 2 --output-dir geyser --overwrite-output 
2018-08-14 10:45:32.160 INFO [progress] - Running: 0, Failed: 0, Done: 0
2018-08-14 10:45:32.161 INFO [thread01] - Warming up
2018-08-14 10:45:32.162 INFO [thread00] - Waiting for warmup to complete
2018-08-14 10:45:37.162 INFO [progress] - Running: 1, Failed: 0, Done: 0
```

- [x] Return value of `.handle` method of ShinySession should not be meaningful. Errors should be communicated with an exception

- [x] Check for failures at the end of the ShinySession run-loop instead of at the beginning. This covers the case of the last event failing.

description:

title: Compute default start interval
description:
This change computes the start interval based on the length of the recording and the number of workers. It results in a more natural default load profile.

I also:

* Cleaned up handling of the `--start-interval` argument; it's now parsed as a Long, which is the type it needed to be ultimately anyway (as an argument to `Thread.sleep`)
* Renamed `logPath` to `recording` wherever it made sense, since that's the terminology we're settling on for the input file. (`logPath` stuck originally because it was an "event log")
* Pass the recording around internally as a `File` instead of a `String` path. Now it makes a `File` early in the run, asserts it exists and is a file and not a directory, and passes the `File` along to the relevant places. These places then don't need to have their own checks.

title: Fix SSP playback when auth is PAM
description:
Apache HttpClient after version 4.3 doesn't send client cookies the Domain fields of which aren't set. This fix modifies every cookie before sending it so that its Domain corresponds to the host of the authentication request.

This resolves a `invalid csrf token` error that exhibited itself in SSP when auth was PAM. I don't know why exactly this problem didn't exhibit itself earlier, when auth was anything other than PAM.

I did find that the error message comes from the `csurf` library, so my best guess is that library is only used in the PAM path for some reason.

title: Regression Fixing Bonanza
description:
This PR fixes 2 major regressions, cleans up the authentication-related code a little bit, and makes a few small tweaks.

The fixed regressions are:

1. RSC + auth either stopped working, or never worked with a particular version/configuration that didn't contribute an `rscid` header to HTTP requests for the app URL. Now, we determine it's RSC by looking at the `Server` header, which seems to be more robust.
1. RSC and SSP were broken since https://github.com/rstudio/shinyloadtest/commit/2752c428d7b64e0db2022ee9605a084169895b0b, which started to ignore `o` messages and responses. Because these weren't recorded, shinycannon didn't expect or play them back, and at least RSC would close the websocket prematurely. Since the handling of the `o` message needed to be special-cased anyway because it's not proper JSON, I think it's fine (open to debate) that the special casing has moved to shinycannon, in the form of awareness of the message and how to respond to it. Now, when shinycannon is handed an `o` message, it will respond immediately with `["0#0|o|"]` before any further interpretation.
    * This new behavior would break pre-subapp versions of SSP, because they would expect `["0|o|"]`

The tweaks are:

* Removed some unused imports
* Changed the `workers` output subdir to `sessions`. This was originally called `sessions` but I changed it to `workers` when we changed the command line argument to `workers` instead of `sessions`, but I realized doing this that `sessions` was still the best name.

## Dev items

* [x] Confirm RSC sniff method with RSC team
  * I learned about `__api__/server_settings` and `__ping__` endpoints from Scott and Uriel, but I think the `Server` header way we're using is fine.
* [x] Confirm RSC auth method with RSC team
  * Learned from Scott the relevant part of Connect is this, and is unlikely to change anytime soon: https://github.com/rstudio/connect/blob/f393b5e64dd03e70fef21f291ee550499fcae16b/src/connect/auth/login/login.go#L45-L51

Using rstudio/shinyloadtest@e76f613 to make recordings:

* [x] Test RSC (1.6.0-9)
* [x] Test SSP (1.5.7)
* [x] Test local

title: Upgrade log format
description:
This makes the following code-review related updates:

* Upgrades `shinycannon` so it can consume logs generated with the very latest version of `shinyloadtest`. The biggest difference is around support for POST requests, which was previously special-cased to the upload input. Now, POST support is general, so any kind of POST can be recorded and played back (such as DT-widget ajax requests)
* Updates the version of Kotlin to 1.2.51 from 1.2.41 - nothing changed here that required our code to change.
* Output CSV files now contain leading session id, worker id, and iteration columns. Previously, only session id was stored. Session id is still a global counter, that increases by one every time a new session - an instance of a playback of a recording - is started. However, there is now a concept of worker and iteration, because the implementation of running sessions has changed. Instead of starting a thread per session, we now start n worker threads, each of which will run 1 or more sessions for some number of *iterations*. All of this information is potentially interesting during analysis, so we included the ids in output. Session CSV file names also change, from `<session>.csv` to `<session>_<worker>_<iteration>.csv`
* There isn't a warning anymore if the recording is too short to span a desired duration, because the workers loop the recording.
* `--loaded-duration-minutes` can be fractional
* Minor cleanup here and there. Many TODOs left from code review remain, notably better error handling. I decided to keep those for another PR.

In addition, the following enhancements were made:

* `--sessions` was changed to `--workers`, and documentation was updated everywhere to reflect the fact that a worker and a session are separate things.
* The `log-path` positional argument became `recording-path`, and the "input log" is referred to instead in documentation as the "recording file produced by shinyloadtest"
* The input recording is copied to the output directory before playback begins, to aid reproducibility, as `recording.log`
